claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record, based on aggregate readiness and public AI governance guidance, while treating the unresolved tax filing assistant materiality and disclosure dispute as a caveat rather than a blocker.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
If the limitation is material, certification requires either disclosure before launch or approved risk acceptance before launch.
General public AI governance principles can support monitoring and documentation practices, but they do not substitute for satisfaction of the internal release policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the tax filing assistant gap must be disclosed before launch.
Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering this named launch use case if disclosure will not be made.
The actual launch model card or disclosure text showing the limitation is disclosed, if such disclosure has been completed.
Any documented materiality decision applying the stated policy text to this named launch use case and partner-commitment context.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness, but not policy compliance for certification if the unresolved weakness is material.
The affected tax filing assistant segment is a named launch use case tied to two partner commitments, which fits the policy text for materiality.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, and no final legal answer, disclosure artifact, or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 6% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality under the policy text provided.
The actor packet overreaches by moving from general readiness and public governance principles to a certification recommendation without the required support link on disclosure or risk acceptance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That the unresolved disclosure sufficiency issue can be preserved merely as a caveat rather than treated as an unresolved policy predicate.
That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are sufficient to satisfy the release policy despite the open materiality dispute.
